uncited: The method evaluates reconstruction quality by computing statistical moments (variance) of outputs generated under specific perturbations, alongside standard fidelity and naturalness metrics.
- A set of input images (or a single image for multiple runs).
- A trained inverse rendering model (e.g., diffusion-based prior) capable of stochastic sampling.
- Ground truth data (albedo, ORM, HDR environment maps) if available for fidelity metrics.
- Standard fidelity metrics (PSNR, SSIM, L1, MSE).
- List of $K$ reconstructed albedo maps $\{A_1, A_2, \dots, A_K\}$ for identical input.
- List of $M$ reconstructed albedo maps $\{B_1, B_2, \dots, B_M\}$ for varied illumination inputs.
- List of $N$ reconstructed environment maps $\{E_1, E_2, \dots, E_N\}$.
Run the inverse rendering model $K$ times (typically $K=5$) on the exact same input image to obtain albedo estimates $A_k$.
where $\bar{A}(\mathbf{p}) = \frac{1}{K} \sum_{k=1}^K A_k(\mathbf{p})$ is the mean albedo at pixel $\mathbf{p}$.
Report the mean $\sigma^2_{\text{sample}}$ over all pixels.
Generate albedo estimates under different illumination conditions (e.g., varying lighting priors or inputs).
Compare the distribution of reconstructed environment maps $\{E_i\}$ to the unconditional distribution of environment maps in the training data corpus.
- Do not blindly minimize $\sigma^2_{\text{invar}}$ or maximize $\sigma^2_{\text{sample}}$.
- **Time Complexity:** Requires $K$ forward passes for sample diversity and $M$ passes for invariance, making evaluation $O(K+M)$ times slower than a single inference pass.
- **Memory Complexity:** Requires storing $K$ or $M$ full-resolution albedo/illumination maps simultaneously for variance computation.
